newsitem.title: BULGARIA: Slovak fund boosts hopes of ex-Mollovbank clients.
newsitem.headline: Slovak fund boosts hopes of ex-Mollovbank clients.

text.p: Depositors in Bulgaria's private Mollovbank, which was placed in receivership last year, should be able to recover their deposits now that Slovak investment fund Istrocapital has bought a 92 percent stake, the bank said.
Board chairman Assen Hristov told a news conference the bank had been renamed Eurobank following Istrocapital's $6.25 million investment.
"Individuals and firms will be able to withdraw their deposits once the bank opens its doors," Hristov said.

He said the bank would be able to cover its liabilities amounting to around $6 million to depositors and to the State Savings Bank. He said bank assets totalled around $10 million, most of them covered by property and other collateral.
A central bank official on Tuesday wrongly described Istrocapital as a Czech investment fund.
Eurobank is expected to boost its capital to 10.7 billion levs from the current 800 million levs through a new share issue, which would improve its capital adequacy ratio.

The Bulgarian National Bank (BNB) put Mollovbank in receivership, dismissed its management and appointed sequestrators on September 23 to prevent its insolvency, citing a negative capital-to-assets ratio of 19 percent and outstanding debt of 22 million levs.
On October 31 the BNB filed a bankruptcy suit against Mollovbank, saying the bank's performing assets were not large enough to cover its liabilities.
A BNB official said on Tuesday the central bank would withdraw the insolvency suit in view of the fresh investment.
Since last May the BNB has filed insolvency suits against 16 state and private banks.
So far only two banks -- Madan-based Krystalbank which stopped operating in November 1995, and the state-owned Mineralbank -- have been declared bankrupt. -- Sofia Newsroom, 359-2-84561
